subject: Request: promo credit issuance flagged — strange signup UA/IP pattern
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@vectorlabs.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Promo credit request — multiple trial accounts (VectorLabs)

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the quick onboarding last week. We started connecting team members and noticed several trial accounts were created automatically and granted the self-serve credits your docs mention. A handful of those accounts have suspicious-looking emails (rotating numeric prefixes, disposable domains) and identical user-agent strings in the logs.

We already rate-limited a few sessions client-side, but the team still needs the credits to run integration tests. Can you confirm whether these trials were manually approved on your side or issued automatically? If auto-issued, is there a way to pause or revoke them while we investigate? I attached a small CSV with the signup rows we pulled.

Appreciate any help — we want to avoid wasting credits if these are bot signups.

—Maya
Product Ops, VectorLabs
From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@vectorlabs.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Promo credit request — multiple trial accounts (VectorLabs)

Hi Maya — thanks for the heads up and the CSV.

Short answer: self-serve credits are normally auto-issued, but we have fraud signals that can block or quarantine issuance. I grabbed your file and flagged it to the Trust queue. Can you confirm: were the signups within a 30-minute window? Also any shared IP ranges from your side?

We should be able to pause additional auto-issuance for your org while we triage. Ben, can we hold further grant issuance on VectorLabs until we finish the check? Dev — can you run the usual UA/IP churn detection against the attached rows and share the sample user-agent strings?

I'll keep Maya in the loop.

Best,
Jasmine
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T12:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Promo credit request — multiple trial accounts (VectorLabs)

Putting this on the temporary hold list now — I set the VectorLabs org id to manual-review for self-serve grants. No further credits should auto-issue.

I also pulled the initial eligibility events and see ~18 signups from 3 closely clustered IPs (external ASN lookups point to a cloud provider in APAC), and ~12 accounts share near-identical UA strings with minute-to-minute timestamps. Looks like a scripted batch. Could be valid internal tests but flags are high.

Marissa, can CS reach out to confirm if VectorLabs is running automated integration checks? If they say no, we'll treat it as abuse and revoke the suspicious grants.

—Ben
Senior Sales Ops
From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T14:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Promo credit request — multiple trial accounts (VectorLabs)

Attached UA sample (ua-sample-headers.txt) — examples: 'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; rv:1.2.3) RedwoodBot/1.0', 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) Chrome/99.0.0.0 RedwoodTest/0.4' — same accept-language and accept-encoding values. Also correlating with signup trace IDs in the S3 path I added to related_links.

Plan:
- Revoke credits for accounts matching IP/UA patterns (manual revoke endpoint)
- Lock account creation for the org for 24 hours (prevent more auto-issuance)
- Ask VectorLabs to verify test runner IPs or provide an allowlist if these are legitimate internal runs

If CS confirms legitimate, we can reinstate credits and whitelist the IP range. Otherwise proceed with revokes and a short account ban.

—Dev
Trust & Safety Eng
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@vectorlabs.com>, jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-13T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Promo credit request — multiple trial accounts (VectorLabs)

Hi Maya — quick note from CS: they confirmed VectorLabs did run internal integration tests late-night last week, but those tests should have come from their staging IPs, not from the cloud provider range Dev flagged. They asked for a short grace period while they pull internal logs.

Proposed compromise: we keep the manual-review hold and revoke credits only for accounts that definitely match the churn/UA signature (we'll mark them as revoked in HubSpot so billing/renewal teams don't restore them). We'll pause mass revocation until VectorLabs confirms. Does that work for you?

—Marissa
Customer Success
From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@vectorlabs.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-14T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Promo credit request — multiple trial accounts (VectorLabs)

Thanks everyone — final steps:
- VectorLabs: please share the staging IP list or confirm which signups were your runners (reply to this thread).
- Dev: revoke the 8 accounts that match the UA/IP fingerprint and tag them in HubSpot with TRST-942. Please attach the revoke audit IDs.
- Marissa: hold any escalation to billing; we'll avoid applying refunds until we confirm.

Maya — once we have your confirmation, we'll either reinstate credits for legitimate tests or proceed with revokes and a short block window. We aim to minimize disruption while protecting credit issuance.

Best,
Jasmine
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
